2. Delayed Registration of Certificate of Live Birth

When the birth of a child is reported for registration after the thirty (30) days reglementary period or those who
have no existing record from the Local Civil Registrar and PSA.

2.1 Out-of-Town Delayed Registration Pursuant to Rule 20 of Administrative Order No.1, Series of 1993-
The process of registering a Certificate of Live Birth of a person born outside of Legazpi City and have no
existing record from the Local Civil Registrar and PSA.

2.2 Delayed Registration under Birth Registration Assistance Project (BRAP)- is a program of Philippine
Statistics Authority (PSA) that aims to increased birth registration in marginalized communities such as
Indigenous People (IPs), Muslim Filipinos, and the poorest sector in the country.

Office or Division:    Birth Registration Section

Classification:        Complex

Type of Transaction:   G2C-Government to Client

Who may avail:         General Public, Government and Private Hospital and Lying-in/ other birth

3. Legitimation

       Process by which a child is granted by law of being legitimate, by legal fiction and upon
       compliance of certain requirements; This is a Legal Instrument on legitimation of a child
       by subsequent marriage of parents, where the birth of child was registered

Type of Transaction:      G2C-Government to Client

   Civil Registrar including those who have blurred/ unreadable copies.

certificate) - 2 certified photocopies

4. Petioner’s personal documents bearing the correct items in reference to his civil
registry documents sought to be corrected - 2 certified photocopies
(e.g. Baptismal certificate; School Records, Driver’s License/ IDs/ Certificate of
Marriage/ Children’s COLB, BIR Record, SSS/Pag-Ibig Record, Passbook/Bankbook)

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR Correction of Gender/Sex/ Date of Month
and Birth Date per Rule 7.1 of RA 10172

1. Certified true copy of the Certificate or certified transcription of the certified true copy
of the page of the registry book containing the entry/ies sought to be corrected/change.

2. Earliest school record/ school documents/ affidavit that the document owner never
entered school (Elementary and High School)

3. Medical record/ Baptismal certificate

4. Baptismal certificate/affidavit if none; other documents issued by religious authorities

5. Clearance or certification that the owner of the document has no pending
administrative, civil or criminal case or no criminal record, which shall be obtained from
the following:
5.1 Employer if employed/ Affidavit of non-employment/self employment
5.2 National Bureau of Investigation
5.3 Philippine National Police

6. Affidavit of Publication from the publisher that the petition has been published for at
least once a week for two(2) consecutive weeks, and a copy of the newspaper clipping

7. Notice and certificate of Posting

8. Certification issued by the City/Municipal Health Officer where the petition for the
correction on the entry of sex was filed certifying that the petitioner has not undergone
sex change or sex transplant

5.Additional documents which the petitioner or the Local Civil Registrar may consider
relevant and necessary for the approval of the petition
